text:
Get it wrong and the patient gets worse. On purpose.

In most medical education, a wrong answer turns red and you move on. Nothing happens to anyone. The stakes are always zero.

But zero stakes produce zero learning at the level that matters.

Here, something happens. Miss the bleed and the pressure keeps falling. Push the wrong drug and the rhythm changes. The physiology responds the way biology says it must.

And you remember it. Not because someone told you it was wrong. Because you watched it cost something.

That is how Caleb taught me. Not by correcting my mistakes from a distance. By letting me see what the mistake produced. The joint that did not hold. The line that was not true. The consequence was the lesson.

The room that can hold your failures is the room where you actually learn.
